mcqs.learning_point: Identify the basic components of an electric circuit
mcqs.question: Which of the following lists all the basic components required to make a complete electric circuit?

options.A: Battery, bulb, switch, and connecting wires
options.B: Battery, bulb, and connecting wires only
options.C: Bulb, switch, and connecting wires only

mcqs.answer: Battery, bulb, switch, and connecting wires
mcqs.explanation: A complete electric circuit needs a source of energy (battery), a load (bulb), a means to control the flow (switch), and conducting paths (wires). Options B, C, and D miss one of these essential parts.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the purpose of a cell or battery
mcqs.question: A student inserts a new cell into a flashlight and the bulb lights up. What is the main purpose of the cell in this circuit?

options.A: To store electrical energy and provide a potential difference
options.B: To act as a switch that opens and closes the circuit

mcqs.answer: To store electrical energy and provide a potential difference
mcqs.explanation: The cell (or battery) is the source of electrical energy; it creates a voltage that drives current through the circuit. It does not function as a switch, connector, or light source.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the function of a switch
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the function of a switch in an electric circuit?

options.A: It opens or closes the circuit to start or stop the flow of current
options.B: It stores electrical energy for later use
options.C: It converts electrical energy into light
options.D: It reduces the voltage supplied by the battery

mcqs.answer: It opens or closes the circuit to start or stop the flow of current
mcqs.explanation: A switch’s role is to make or break the conducting path, thereby controlling whether current can flow. It does not store energy, emit light, or change voltage.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the role of connecting wires
mcqs.question: If the connecting wires in a simple circuit are broken, what will happen to the bulb?

options.A: The bulb will not light because the circuit becomes open and current cannot flow
options.B: The bulb will become brighter because the resistance decreases
options.C: The battery will discharge faster even though the bulb stays lit
options.D: The switch will automatically close to complete the circuit

mcqs.answer: The bulb will not light because the circuit becomes open and current cannot flow
mcqs.explanation: Wires provide the continuous path for current. A break makes the circuit open, stopping current flow, so the bulb remains off. The other options describe effects that do not occur with a broken wire.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish an open circuit from a closed circuit
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an open circuit from a closed circuit?

options.A: In an open circuit the path is broken so no current flows; in a closed circuit the path is complete and current flows.
options.B: In an open circuit current flows freely; in a closed circuit current is blocked.
options.C: Both open and closed circuits allow current, but an open circuit has higher voltage.
options.D: An open circuit always has higher resistance than a closed circuit, regardless of components.

mcqs.answer: In an open circuit the path is broken so no current flows; in a closed circuit the path is complete and current flows.
mcqs.explanation: The defining difference is continuity of the path. An open circuit lacks continuity, preventing current; a closed circuit provides continuity, allowing current. Options B, C, and D misstate the fundamental distinction.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent simple circuits using appropriate symbols
mcqs.question: Which diagram correctly represents a simple series circuit that contains a battery, a switch, and a bulb?

options.A: A single loop showing the battery symbol followed by a switch symbol and then a bulb symbol, all connected end‑to‑end.
options.B: A battery symbol with two parallel branches, each containing a bulb symbol.
options.C: A battery symbol followed by a switch symbol, then two bulb symbols placed in series.
options.D: A battery symbol with an open switch symbol (gap) and no bulb symbol.

mcqs.answer: A single loop showing the battery symbol followed by a switch symbol and then a bulb symbol, all connected end‑to‑end.
mcqs.explanation: A simple series circuit is drawn as one continuous loop where the components appear one after another. Option A matches this description. Options B and C show parallel or extra components, and D lacks the required load (bulb).

mcqs.learning_point: Identify the basic components of an electric circuit
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a basic component of a simple electric circuit?
mcqs.explanation: For a simple circuit, the essential parts are a source (battery), a load (bulb), a conductor (wire), and optionally a switch. A resistor is an additional component used to control current, not a basic requirement.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the purpose of a cell or battery
mcqs.question: What is the primary purpose of a cell or battery in an electric circuit?

options.A: To provide the source of electrical energy by creating a potential difference
options.B: To act as a conductor that connects other components
options.C: To function as a switch that opens and closes the circuit
options.D: To convert electrical energy directly into light

mcqs.answer: To provide the source of electrical energy by creating a potential difference
mcqs.explanation: A cell or battery converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy, establishing a voltage that drives current through the circuit. It does not serve as a conductor, switch, or light source.
